rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What a person earns of good is for that person as reward and recompense.
rows.anchor: ما عملت من الخير، لها أجره وثوابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What a person acquires of evil is against that person, carrying its burden.
rows.anchor: من الشر وعليها وزره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plea asks God not to punish the believers.
rows.anchor: أي لا تعاقبنا

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi reads forgetfulness as actual forgetting: Israelites who forgot or erred were punished at once, sometimes by losing foods; believers were taught to ask for no such reckoning.
rows.anchor: قال الكلبي كانت بنو إسرائيل إذا نسوا شيئا مما أمروا به أو أخطأوا عجلت لهم العقوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes forgetting to mean neglecting or abandoning God, as in the verse saying they forgot God and He forgot them.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو من النسيان الذي هو الترك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view says the word for erring can mean acting deliberately, supported by its use for a grave intentional act elsewhere.
rows.anchor: قيل معناه القصد والعمد يقال

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: ʿAta interprets the plea as covering ignorance and deliberate action.
rows.anchor: قال عطاء: إن نسينا أو أخطأنا يعني

rows.speaker: الأكثرون
rows.claim: Most interpreters take error as ignorance or inadvertence: deliberate sin is not simply absolved, but left to God’s will, whereas error is forgiven.
rows.anchor: وجعله الأكثرون من الخطإ الذي هو الجهل والسهو، لأن ما كان عمدا من الذنب فغير معفو عنه

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet said that error, forgetfulness, and coercion have been lifted from his community.
rows.anchor: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: "رفع عن أمتي الخطأ والنسيان وما

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid, ʿAta, Qatada, al-Suddi, al-Kalbi, and others say the burden is a severe covenant the Israelites could not fulfill and were punished for breaking; the wording is supported by the covenant verse.
rows.anchor: هذا قول مجاهد وعطاء وقتادة والسدي والكلبي وجماعة

rows.speaker: عثمان
rows.claim: A second view, attributed to ʿUthman, ʿAta, Malik, Abu ʿUbayda, and others, asks that the law not be made as severe as it was for earlier Jews: fifty prayers, a quarter of wealth in alms, cutting away impurity from clothes, and sins displayed on the door; the author links this to the verse about removing burdens.
rows.anchor: وهذا معنى قول عثمان وعطاء ومالك بن أنس وأبي عبيدة وجماعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation calls the burden a sin for which there is no repentance and takes the plea to ask protection from such a sin.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الإصر ذنب لا توبة له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word’s underlying sense is restraint and binding firmly.
rows.anchor: والأصل فيه العقل والإحكام

words: ولا تحملنا ما لا طاقة لنا به
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The petition asks not to be charged with deeds beyond their capacity.
rows.anchor: أي لا تكلفنا من الأعمال ما لا نطيقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed view takes the unbearable burden to mean inner speech and whispering.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو حديث النفس والوسوسة

rows.speaker: مكحول
rows.claim: Makḥul identifies the burden as intense sexual desire.
rows.anchor: حكي عن مكحول أنه قال: هو الغلمة

rows.speaker: إبراهيم
rows.claim: Ibrahim says the burden is love.
rows.anchor: وعن إبراهيم قال: هو الحب

rows.speaker: محمد بن عبد الوهاب
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhab identifies it as passionate love.
rows.anchor: وعن محمد بن عبد الوهاب قال: العشق

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj says it means transformation into apes and swine.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن جريج: هو مسخ القردة والخنازير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed explanation identifies the burden as the gloating of enemies.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو شماتة الأعداء، وقيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another unnamed explanation identifies it as separation and estrangement.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو الفرقة والقطيعة نعوذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The request is that God overlook and erase their sins.
rows.anchor: أي تجاوز وامح عنا ذنوبنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The request is that God cover their sins and not expose them.
rows.anchor: استر علينا ذنوبنا ولا تفضحنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They cannot attain good action except through obedience granted by God, nor leave disobedience except through His mercy.
rows.anchor: فإننا لا ننال العمل إلا بطاعتك، ولا نترك معصيتك إلا برحمتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is their helper, protector, and patron.
rows.anchor: {أنت مولانا} ناصرنا وحافظنا وولينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final plea asks God to grant victory over the disbelieving people.
rows.anchor: فانصرنا على القوم الكافرين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas, in a report from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, says God answered the closing pleas with forgiveness, pardon, mercy, and victory.
rows.anchor: روى سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما

rows.speaker: معاذ بن جبل
rows.claim: Muʿadh ibn Jabal would say amen when he completed Surat al-Baqara.
rows.anchor: وكان معاذ بن جبل إذا ختم سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: ʿAbd Allah reports that during the night journey the Prophet reached the lote tree in the sixth heaven, received the five prayers and closing verses of al-Baqara, and was granted forgiveness for members of his community who did not associate partners with God.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله قال: لما أسري برسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wife of ʿImran is Hanna daughter of Qafudha, Mary’s mother; this ʿImran is Ibn Mathan, not the father of Moses, with 1,080 years between them.
rows.anchor: وهي حنة بنت قافوذا أم مريم، وعمران هو عمران بن ماثان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another identification gives Mary’s father’s name as ʿImran ibn Ashham.
rows.anchor: وقيل: عمران بن أشهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A vow is something a person makes obligatory upon themself.
rows.anchor: والنذر: ما يوجبه الإنسان على نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She dedicated the child as free for God, wholly devoted to worship and temple service, with no worldly occupation; anything sincerely devoted is called muḥarrar.
rows.anchor: أي عتيقا خالصا لله مفرغا لعبادة الله ولخدمة الكنيسة لا أشغله بشيء من الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word also evokes freeing a slave from bondage.
rows.anchor: يقال: حررت العبد إذا أعتقته وخلصته من الرق

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi, Muhammad ibn Ishaq, and others describe the temple dedication: boys served and cleaned the church until puberty, then could choose to stay or leave; only boys were dedicated because girls experienced menstruation and its effects.
rows.anchor: قال الكلبي ومحمد بن إسحاق وغيرهما: كان المحرر إذا حرر جعل في الكنيسة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account says Zakariya and ʿImran married sisters: Ashiya, mother of Yahya, married Zakariya; Hanna, Mary’s mother, married ʿImran. Their family held a high standing with God.
rows.anchor: وكانت أشياع بنت قافوذا أم يحيى عند زكريا، وكانت حنة بنت قافوذا أم مريم عند عمران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hanna had remained childless into old age; seeing a bird feed its chick stirred her longing, and she prayed for a child, vowing to give it to Jerusalem as a temple attendant.
rows.anchor: فبينما هي في ظل شجرة بصرت بطائر يطعم فرخا فتحركت بذلك نفسها للولد

words: نذرت لك ما في بطني محررا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After conceiving Mary, Hanna consecrated the child without knowing its sex; ʿImran objected that a girl could not serve, and both were distressed; ʿImran died while she was pregnant.
rows.anchor: فحملت بمريم فحررت ما في بطنها، ولم تعلم ما هو فقال لها زوجها:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God accepted Mary from Hanna in place of the male child expected for temple service; acceptance means receiving and approving.
rows.anchor: أي تقبل الله مريم من حنة مكان المحرر، وتقبل بمعنى قبل ورضي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation takes acceptance to mean undertaking her upbringing and care.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معنى التقبل التكفل في التربية والقيام بشأنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qabul is the verbal noun of accepting; the source compares it with the uncommon forms wuluʿ and wuzaʿ.
rows.anchor: والقبول مصدر قبل يقبل قبولا مثل الولوع والوزوع ولم يأت غير هذه الثلاثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording uses an unmatching verbal noun: God made her grow, and she grew well.
rows.anchor: معناه: وأنبتها فنبتت نباتا حسنا وقيل هذا مصدر على غير

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Juwaybir reports from al-Dahhak, from Ibn ʿAbbas, that God led Mary along the path of the blessed.
rows.anchor: وقال جويبر عن الضحاك عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation says her body was formed evenly, without excess or deficiency, and she grew in one day what an infant ordinarily grows in a year.
rows.anchor: يعني سوى خلقها من غير زيادة ولا نقصان فكانت تنبت في اليوم ما ينبت المولود في العام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hanna wrapped Mary and brought her to the temple priests, Aaron’s descendants who managed the sanctuary; they competed to care for her because she was the daughter of their leader and offerer.
rows.anchor: أخذت حنة مريم حين ولدتها فلفتها في خرقة وحملتها إلى المسجد فوضعتها عند الأحبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakariya claimed her because he had her maternal aunt; the priests instead proposed casting lots, and twenty-nine men went to a flowing river.
rows.anchor: فقال لهم زكريا: أنا أحقكم بها، عندي خالتها، فقالت له الأحبار: لا نفعل ذلك

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi identifies the river as the Jordan; the pens were cast in water, and whoever’s pen stayed and rose was to have first claim.
rows.anchor: قال السدي: هو نهر الأردن فألقوا أقلامهم في الماء على أن من ثبت قلمه في الماء فصعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account says each pen bore the name of one of the competing priests.
rows.anchor: وقيل: كان على كل قلم اسم واحد منهم

rows.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn Ishaq and others say the priests cast the pens with which they wrote the Torah; Zakariya’s pen stood and rose above the water while the others sank.
rows.anchor: قاله محمد بن إسحاق وجماعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account says Zakariya’s pen ran upstream while the other pens followed the water’s course.
rows.anchor: وقيل: جرى قلم زكريا مصعدا إلى أعلى الماء وجرت أقلامهم بجري الماء

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi and others instead say Zakariya’s pen stood upright in the water as if in clay, while the others flowed with the current; he won the lot.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي وجماعة: بل ثبت قلم زكريا وقام فوق الماء كأنه في طين، وجرت أقلامهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakariya was the head priest and their prophet, and the lot selected him to take Mary into his care.
rows.anchor: فسهمهم وقرعهم زكريا، وكان زكريا رأس الأحبار ونبيهم

rows.speaker: حمزة
rows.claim: Hamza, al-Kisaʾi, and ʿAsim read the verb with a doubled f; Zakariya is accusative, with God assigning Mary to his care through the lot.
rows.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي وعاصم بتشديد الفاء فيكون زكريا في محل النصب أي ضمنها الله زكريا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The other readers use a light f; Zakariya is nominative as the one who took Mary in and cared for her.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الآخرون بالتخفيف فيكون زكريا في محل الرفع أي ضمها زكريا إلى نفسه وقام بأمرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakariya is identified as son of Adhan, son of Muslim, son of Saduq, from the line of Solomon and David.
rows.anchor: وهو زكريا بن آذن بن مسلم بن صدوق، من أولاد سليمان بن داود عليهما السلام

rows.speaker: حمزة
rows.claim: Hamza, al-Kisaʾi, and Hafs from ʿAsim shorten the name Zakariya; the other readers lengthen it.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم: زكريا مقصورا والآخرون يمدونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After taking Mary in, Zakariya built her a house and arranged a wet nurse; Ibn Ishaq says he placed her with her aunt Umm Yahya until she matured, then built her a chamber in the mosque reached by a ladder.
rows.anchor: فلما ضم زكريا مريم إلى نفسه بنى لها، بيتا واسترضع لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mihrab can mean an upper room, the most honored and foremost place in an assembly, or a mosque.
rows.anchor: وأراد بالمحراب الغرفة، والمحراب أشرف المجالس ومقدمها، وكذلك هو من المسجد

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrid says a mihrab must be elevated by a step.
rows.anchor: قال المبرد: لا يكون المحراب إلا أن يرتقى إليه بدرجة

rows.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
rows.claim: Al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas says Zakariya locked seven doors when he left Mary in her upper chamber.
rows.anchor: وقال الربيع بن أنس: كان زكريا إذا خرج يغلق عليها سبعة أبواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The provision was fruit appearing out of season: summer fruit in winter and winter fruit in summer.
rows.anchor: أي فاكهة في غير حينها، فاكهة الصيف في الشتاء وفاكهة الشتاء في الصيف

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu ʿUbayda explains the question as asking where the food came from.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة: معناه من أين لك هذا؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some object to Abu ʿUbayda: anna asks from what direction, while aina asks about a place.
rows.anchor: وأنكر بعضهم عليه، وقال: معناه من أي جهة لك هذا؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation says Mary’s food came from the fruit of Paradise.
rows.anchor: أي من قطف الجنة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says Mary never suckled; her food came from Paradise, and she spoke while still very young.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن: حين ولدت مريم لم تلقم ثديا قط، كان يأتيها رزقها من الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative refers to the accounts just given of Zakariya, Yahya, Mary, and Jesus.
rows.anchor: {ذلك} الذي ذكرت من حديث زكريا ويحيى ومريم وعيسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These are reports of the unseen that God reveals to Muhammad.
rows.anchor: من أخبار الغيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in the revelation verb refers back to dhalika, which accounts for its masculine form.
rows.anchor: رد الكناية إلى ذلك فلذلك ذكره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their pens were casting lots in water to decide who would care for Mary.
rows.anchor: سهامهم في الماء للاقتراع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question is which person would take Mary in, raise her, and care for her.
rows.anchor: يحضنها ويربيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dispute among them concerned who would have custody of Mary.
rows.anchor: وما كنت لديهم إذ يختصمون} في كفالتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The occasion was the People of the Book each claiming Abraham’s religion and disputing before the Prophet; when he said neither group followed Abraham’s religion, they rejected his judgment and religion, and the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: فادعى كل واحد أنه على دين إبراهيم عليه السلام واختصموا إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abu Jaʿfar, the Basrans, and Hafs from ʿAsim read the verb in the third person, matching the later reference to those who are defiantly disobedient.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر وأهل البصرة وحفص عن عاصم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The other readers use the second person, matching the second person in the preceding address.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الآخرون بالتاء لقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To submit here means to yield and comply.
rows.anchor: خضع وانقاد، {من في السماوات والأرض طوعا وكرها}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Willing submission is easy obedience; coerced submission involves difficulty and resistance of the self.
rows.anchor: فالطوع: الانقياد والاتباع بسهولة، والكره: ما كان بمشقة وإباء من النفس

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says the inhabitants of heaven submit willingly, while people on earth include willing believers and those compelled by fear of the sword and captivity.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن: أسلم أهل السموات طوعا وأسلم من في الأرض بعضهم طوعا وبعضهم كرها

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid identifies willing submission with the believer and coerced submission with the unbeliever, citing the verse that says all bow to God willingly or unwillingly.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: طوعا المؤمن، وكرها ذلك الكافر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view places this submission at the primordial covenant, when people answered God’s question about His lordship, some willingly and some unwillingly.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هذا يوم الميثاق حين قال لهم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the believer submits willingly and benefits, while the unbeliever’s coerced submission at the moment of danger is useless, as the verse about seeing punishment shows.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: المؤمن أسلم طوعا فنفعه، والكافر أسلم كرها في وقت البأس فلم ينفعه

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Shaʿbi takes coerced submission as people calling sincerely upon God in distress, such as sailors in a storm.
rows.anchor: وقال الشعبي: هو استعاذتهم به عند اضطرارهم

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says the willing are those born into Islam and the coerced are captives forced into Islam in chains.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي: طوعا الذي {ولد}

rows.speaker: حفص عن عاصم
rows.claim: Hafs from ʿAsim and Yaʿqub read the final verb in the third person; most use second person for both verbs, while Abu ʿAmr uses third person first and second person here because the first is specific and the return to God is universal.
rows.anchor: قرأ بالياء حفص عن عاصم ويعقوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God wants to accept your repentance if you fall short in religious duties.
rows.anchor: إن وقع منكم تقصير في أمر دينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those following desires want believers to turn far from the truth by committing what God prohibited.
rows.anchor: عن الحق، {ميلا عظيما} بإتيانكم ما حرم عليكم

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi identifies those who follow desires as Jews and Christians.
rows.anchor: قال السدي: هم اليهود والنصارى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view identifies them as Magians, who permit marriage to sisters and nieces.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم: هم المجوس لأنهم يحلون نكاح الأخوات وبنات الأخ والأخت

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says they are adulterers who want others to leave the truth and fornicate as they do.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: هم الزناة يريدون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A broader view includes all people committed to falsehood.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هم جميع أهل الباطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God intends to make the rules of religious law easier for you; the author links this to the verse about removing burdens.
rows.anchor: يسهل عليكم في أحكام الشرع، وقد سهل كما قال جل ذكره: "ويضع عنهم إصرهم"

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet described his mission as bringing the upright, tolerant, and easy religion.
rows.anchor: وقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: "بعثت بالحنيفية السمحة السلهة"

rows.speaker: طاووس
rows.claim: Tawus and al-Kalbi explain human weakness in relation to women: a person cannot patiently abstain from them.
rows.anchor: قال طاووس والكلبي وغيرهما في أمر النساء: لا يصبر عنهن

rows.speaker: ابن كيسان
rows.claim: Ibn Kaysan says desire and appetite draw a person toward what is wanted.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن كيسان: {وخلق الإنسان ضعيفا} يستميله هواه وشهوته

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says human weakness refers to being created from lowly fluid, as another verse states.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: هو أنه خلق من ماء مهين، بيانه قوله تعالى: "الله الذي خلقكم من ضعف"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition covers unlawful wealth-taking, including usury, gambling, usurpation, theft, and treachery; another view includes invalid contracts.
rows.anchor: بالحرام، يعني: بالربا والقمار والغصب والسرقة والخيانة

rows.speaker: أهل الكوفة
rows.claim: The Kufans read trade in the accusative as the predicate of kāna, meaning the property becomes trade.
rows.anchor: قرأ أهل الكوفة {تجارة} نصب على خبر كان،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The other readers use the nominative, taking the phrase to mean that a trade occurs.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الآخرون بالرفع، أي: إلا أن تقع تجارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Valid trade requires the good will of each party.
rows.anchor: أي: بطيبة نفس كل واحد منكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says each buyer may ratify the other’s sale; until they separate, either may rescind, after which the transaction is binding.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو أن يجيز كل واحد من المتبايعين صاحبه بعد البيع، فيلزم، وإلا فلهما الخيار ما لم يتفرقا

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reports the Prophet saying each of two traders retains the option until they separate, unless the sale is made with the option stipulated.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمر أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "المتبايعان

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas reports that an Ansari, Thaʿma ibn Ubayriq, stole armor from his neighbor Qatada ibn al-Nuʿman, hid it with the Jewish man Zayd al-Samin, and denied the theft under oath; the flour trail led investigators to his house and then to the Jew, who said Thaʿma had given it to him.
rows.anchor: روى الكلبي عن أبي صالح عن ابن عباس قال: نزلت هذه الآية

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In the same report, Thaʿma’s clansmen asked the Prophet to defend him lest he be disgraced, and he was about to punish the Jewish man.
rows.anchor: فجاء بنو ظفر وهم قوم طعمة إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وسألوه أن يجادل عن صاحبهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A second report from Ibn ʿAbbas says Thaʿma left a leaking bran sack at Zayd’s door after taking the armor home; following the bran trail, the owner brought Zayd to the Prophet, who was about to cut the Jew’s hand.
rows.anchor: ويروى عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في رواية أخرى أن طعمة سرق الدرع في جراب فيه نخالة

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil gives a different account: Zayd had entrusted armor to Thaʿma, who then denied possessing it, and the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل: إن زيدا السمين أودع درعا عند طعمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Book was sent with commands, prohibitions, and decisive judgment.
rows.anchor: بالأمر والنهي والفصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is to judge by what God taught him and revealed to him.
rows.anchor: بما علمك الله وأوحى إليك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The treacherous person is Thaʿma, and the command forbids acting as his advocate or defender.
rows.anchor: [طعمة] (2) {خصيما} معينا مدافعا عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sin is Thaʿma’s false oath, by which he claimed that the Jew had stolen the armor; earning the sin harms the person who commits it.
rows.anchor: يعني: يمين طعمة بالباطل، أي: ما سرقته إنما سرقه اليهودي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knew who stole the armor, and His wise judgment imposed the hand-cutting penalty on the thief.
rows.anchor: بسارق الدرع {حكيما} حكم بالقطع على السارق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The error is stealing the armor, the sin is the lying oath, and casting it on an innocent person means accusing the Jew; the resulting slander is an enormous lie and manifest sin.
rows.anchor: أي: سرقة الدرع، {أو إثما} يمينه الكاذبة، {ثم يرم به} أي: يقذف بما جنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Buhtan is a lie so immense that it leaves its hearer bewildered.
rows.anchor: البهتان: هو البهت، وهو الكذب الذي يتحير في عظمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular pronoun after both khatiʾa and ithm either refers back to ithm or treats the error and sin as one thing.
rows.anchor: رد الكناية إلى الإثم، أو جعل الخطيئة والإثم كالشيء الواحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means that a group truly intended to mislead the Prophet; hamma means to intend or resolve.
rows.anchor: يقول للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: {لهمت} لقد همت أي: أضمرت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The group was Thaʿma’s people, who tried to mislead the Prophet about the ruling and confuse the matter so he would defend Thaʿma.
rows.anchor: يعني: قوم طعمة، {أن يضلوك} يخطئوك في الحكم ويلبسوا عليك الأمر

words: وما يضلون إلا أنفسهم وما يضرونك من شيء
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their attempt to mislead harms only themselves; its injury returns to them and does not harm the Prophet.
rows.anchor: يعني يرجع وباله عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Book means the Qurʾan, and wisdom means judgment through revelation.
rows.anchor: وكان فضل الله عليك عظيما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation says God taught the Prophet legal rulings he had not known.
rows.anchor: من الأحكام، وقيل: من علم الغيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation says God taught him knowledge of the unseen.
rows.anchor: الأحكام، وقيل: من علم الغيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two sons of Adam are Habil and Qabil; Qabil is also called Qabin.
rows.anchor: نبأ ابني آدم بالحق} وهما هابيل وقابيل

rows.speaker: أهل العلم
rows.claim: The account says Eve bore one boy and one girl in each of twenty pregnancies, forty children total, from Qabil and his twin Aqlima to ʿAbd al-Mughith and his twin Umm al-Mughith.
rows.anchor: أن حواء كانت تلد لآدم عليه السلام في كل بطن غلاما وجارية

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says Adam lived until his children and grandchildren numbered forty thousand.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: لم يمت آدم حتى بلغ ولده وولد ولده أربعين ألفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account says Qabil and his twin Aqlima were born a hundred years after Adam and Eve descended to earth, followed by Habil and his twin Labuda.
rows.anchor: فقال بعضهم: غشي آدم حواء بعد مهبطهما إلى الأرض بمائة سنة

rows.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn Ishaq, citing scriptural scholars, says Qabil and Aqlima were conceived in Paradise before the sin without pregnancy pains, while Habil and Labuda were conceived after the descent and accompanied by the pains and blood of childbirth.
rows.anchor: وقال محمد بن إسحاق عن بعض أهل العلم بالكتاب الأول: إن آدم كان يغشى حواء في الجنة قبل أن يصيب الخطيئة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the only women were their sisters, Adam’s children married a sister from another twin pair, never their own twin; Qabil and Habil were two years apart, according to al-Kalbi.
rows.anchor: يتزوج أية أخواته شاء إلا توأمته التي ولدت معه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God ordered Qabil to marry Habil’s sister Labuda and Habil to marry Qabil’s sister Aqlima; Qabil objected because his twin was more beautiful, while Habil accepted. Adam said the accepted offering would decide who married her.
rows.anchor: أمر الله تعالى آدم عليه السلام أن ينكح قابيل لبودا أخت هابيل وينكح هابيل أقليما أخت قابيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At that time an accepted offering was consumed by white fire from heaven; a rejected offering was left for birds and beasts.
rows.anchor: وكانت القرابين إذا كانت مقبولة نزلت نار من السماء بيضاء فأكلتها، وإذا لم تكن مقبولة لم تنزل النار وأكلته الطير والسباع

words: فتقبل من أحدهما ولم يتقبل من الآخر
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qabil, a farmer, offered a pile of his poorest grain and inwardly did not care whether God accepted it; Habil, a shepherd, offered his best ram sincerely seeking God’s approval. Fire consumed Habil’s offering alone.
rows.anchor: وكان قابيل صاحب زرع فقرب صبرة من الطعام من أردأ زرعه وأضمر في نفسه ما أبالي أيقبل مني أم لا

words: فتقبل من أحدهما ولم يتقبل من الآخر
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accepted brother is Habil and the rejected one Qabil.
rows.anchor: {ولم يتقبل من الآخر} يعني: قابيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After his offering was rejected, Qabil nursed envy; when Adam left to visit the House in Mecca, Qabil approached Habil among the flock and threatened him, resentful of Habil’s accepted offering and better marriage.
rows.anchor: فلما غاب آدم أتى قابيل هابيل وهو في غنمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qabil explains his threat by saying God accepted Habil’s offering, rejected his, gave Habil the beautiful sister, and left him the plain one, so people and their descendants would consider Habil superior.
rows.anchor: لأن الله تعالى قبل قربانك ورد قرباني، وتنكح أختي الحسناء وأنكح أختك الدميمة، فيتحدث الناس أنك خير مني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Habil answers that he bears no guilt for Qabil’s rejection and that God accepts only from the God-fearing.
rows.anchor: {قال} هابيل: وما ذنبي؟ {إنما يتقبل الله من المتقين}
